subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain economics as a social science
Explain the problem of choice (scarcity, opportunity cost, basic economic questions)
Explain the production possibilities curve (PPC) model and its features
Explain the circular flow of income model
allowed_methods: PPC diagram illustrating choice, opportunity cost, unemployment, efficiency, actual growth, growth in production possibilities
PPC diagram showing increasing vs constant opportunity cost
Circular flow of income model diagram with leakages and injections
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4 for PPC and circular flow

subject: Economics
subtopic: How do economists approach the world?
learning_objectives: Explain the role of positive economics (logic, hypotheses, models, theories, ceteris paribus, empirical evidence, refutation)
Explain the role of normative economics (value judgments, equity vs equality)
Outline the origin of economic ideas in a historical context
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain the law of demand
Draw a demand curve
Explain the relationship between individual and market demand
Explain non-price determinants of demand (income, tastes, future expectations, price of related goods, number of consumers)
Distinguish between movements along and shifts of the demand curve
allowed_methods: Downward-sloping demand curve diagram
Diagram showing movements along and shifts of the demand curve
explicit_exclusions: Assumptions underlying the law of demand (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4 for diagrams

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain the law of supply
Draw a supply curve
Explain the relationship between individual and market supply
Explain non-price determinants of supply (costs of FOPs, prices of related goods, indirect taxes/subsidies, future expectations, technology, number of firms)
Distinguish between movements along and shifts of the supply curve
allowed_methods: Upward-sloping supply curve diagram
Diagram showing movements along and shifts of the supply curve
explicit_exclusions: Assumptions underlying the law of supply (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4 for diagrams

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Illustrate market equilibrium using demand and supply curves
Show how shifts in demand/supply produce a new equilibrium (excess demand/supply)
Explain the functions of the price mechanism (resource allocation: signalling, incentive; rationing)
Explain consumer surplus, producer surplus, and social/community surplus
Explain allocative efficiency at competitive market equilibrium (social surplus maximized, MB=MC)
allowed_methods: Market equilibrium diagram
Diagram showing changes in equilibrium/role of price mechanism
Diagram showing consumer surplus and producer surplus (social/community surplus) maximized at equilibrium
explicit_exclusions: Calculation of consumer/producer surplus from a diagram (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4 for diagrams

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain the concept of elasticity
Define and calculate price elasticity of demand (PED)
Explain the degrees/theoretical range of PED values
Explain determinants of PED (substitutes, necessity, proportion of income, time)
Explain the relationship between PED and total revenue
Explain the importance of PED for firms and government
Define and calculate income elasticity of demand (YED)
Interpret YED values (normal/inferior goods, necessities/luxuries)
allowed_methods: Diagram: relatively elastic/inelastic demand
Diagram: constant PED (perfectly elastic, inelastic, unitary)
Diagram: changes in revenue from price changes when demand is elastic/inelastic
Diagram: Engel curve showing income elastic, inelastic, inferior goods
Calculation: PED, change in price/quantity/total revenue from data
Calculation: YED, change in income/quantity from data
explicit_exclusions: Changing PED along a straight-line demand curve (HL only)
Reasons why PED for primary commodities is lower than for manufactured products (HL only)
Importance of YED for firms and sectoral structure (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO1, AO2, AO4. AO3 for importance of PED.

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Define and calculate price elasticity of supply (PES)
Explain the degrees/theoretical range of PES values
Explain determinants of PES (time, mobility of FOPs, unused capacity, storage, cost increases)
allowed_methods: Diagram: relatively elastic/inelastic supply
Diagram: constant PES (perfectly elastic, inelastic, unitary)
Calculation: PES, change in price/quantity from data
explicit_exclusions: Reasons why PES for primary commodities is lower than for manufactured products (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain reasons for government intervention in markets
Explain main forms of intervention (price controls, indirect taxes/subsidies, direct provision, command/control regulation)
Analyze consequences of government intervention for markets and stakeholders
allowed_methods: Diagram: price ceiling (maximum price)
Diagram: price floor (minimum price)
Diagram: indirect tax
Diagram: subsidy showing effects on markets and stakeholders
explicit_exclusions: Consumer nudges (HL only)
Calculation of effects of price controls/taxes/subsidies on markets/stakeholders (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4 for diagrams, AO3 for consequences

subject: Economics
subtopic: Market failure - externalities and common pool resources
learning_objectives: Define socially optimum output (MSB = MSC, allocative efficiency, social surplus maximized)
Explain positive/negative externalities of production/consumption, welfare loss, merit/demerit goods
Explain common pool resources (characteristics, tragedy of commons, unsustainable production)

Explain government responses to externalities/CPRs (indirect taxes, carbon taxes, legislation, education, tradable permits, international agreements, collective governance, subsidies, government provision)
Evaluate strengths/limitations of government policies to correct externalities/manage CPRs
allowed_methods: Diagram: allocative efficiency
Diagram: market failure due to negative/positive externalities of production/consumption
Diagram: government responses (indirect taxes, subsidies, legislation, education) showing effects on a polluting industry
explicit_exclusions: Calculation of welfare loss from a diagram (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4 for diagrams, AO3 for evaluation

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Define public goods (non-rivalrous, non-excludable) and the free rider problem
Evaluate government intervention for public goods (direct provision, contracting out)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO3

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain national income accounting as a measure of economic activity
Explain equivalence of income, output, expenditure approaches with reference to circular flow model
Define and calculate [nominal] GDP (expenditure approach), [nominal] GNI
Define and calculate real GDP/GNI using a price deflator
Define and calculate real GDP/GNI per capita (PPP)
Explain the business cycle (short-term fluctuations, long-term growth trend)
Evaluate appropriateness of GDP/GNI for measuring economic well-being (comparisons over time/between countries)
Describe alternative measures of well-being (OECD Better Life Index, Happiness Index, Happy Planet Index)
allowed_methods: Diagram: circular flow of income model showing interactions, leakages, injections
Diagram: business cycle showing fluctuations and long-term growth trend
Calculation: nominal GDP from national income data (expenditure approach)
Calculation: nominal GNI from data
Calculation: real GDP/GNI using a price deflator
Calculation: real GDP per capita, real GNI per capita
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4 for calculations/diagrams, AO3 for evaluation

subject: Economics
subtopic: Variations in economic activity - aggregate demand and aggregate supply
learning_objectives: Define aggregate demand (AD) and its components (C+I+G+X-M)
Explain determinants of AD components (C, I, G, X-M)
Illustrate shifts of the AD curve
Explain the short-run aggregate supply (SRAS) curve and its determinants (costs of FOPs, indirect taxes)
Illustrate shifts of the SRAS curve
Explain alternative views of aggregate supply (monetarist/new classical LRAS, Keynesian AS, inflationary/deflationary gaps)
Illustrate shifts of LRAS/Keynesian AS (changes in quantity/quality of FOPs, technology, efficiency, institutions)
Explain macroeconomic equilibrium (short-run, monetarist/new classical long-run at full employment, automatic adjustment, natural rate of unemployment; Keynesian persistence of deflationary gaps)
Compare assumptions/implications of monetarist/new classical and Keynesian models
allowed_methods: Diagram: AD curve
Diagram: shifts of AD curve
Diagram: SRAS curve
Diagram: shifts of SRAS curve
Diagram: alternative views of AS curve
Diagram: shifts of LRAS or Keynesian AS
Diagram: macroeconomic equilibrium in short and long run
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4 for diagrams, AO3 for comparison

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain economic growth (short-term: actual growth in PPC, role of AD; long-term: shifts of PPC, role of LRAS)
Measure economic growth rate from data
Evaluate consequences of economic growth (living standards, environment, income distribution)
Define and measure unemployment and the unemployment rate from data
Explain difficulties measuring unemployment
Explain causes of unemployment (cyclical, structural, seasonal, frictional)
Define natural rate of unemployment
Explain costs of unemployment (personal, social, economic)
Define and measure inflation rate using CPI data
Explain limitations of CPI
Explain causes of inflation (demand-pull, cost-push)
Explain costs of high inflation
Explain causes of deflation (changes in AD/SRAS), disinflation
Explain costs of deflation
Evaluate relative costs of unemployment vs inflation
Evaluate potential conflicts between macroeconomic objectives (unemployment/inflation, growth/inflation, growth/sustainability, growth/equity)
allowed_methods: Diagram: PPC showing actual growth and growth in production possibilities
Diagram: AD increases showing real output increase
Diagram: LRAS increases showing full employment output increase
Diagram: minimum wage showing unemployment
Diagram: fall in demand for labour for a particular market/area
Diagram: deflationary gap showing cyclical unemployment
Diagram: demand-pull inflation
Diagram: cost-push inflation
Diagram: deflation
Calculation: rate of economic growth from data
Calculation: unemployment rate from data
Calculation: inflation rate from data using quantities as weights in CPI
explicit_exclusions: Sustainable level of government debt (HL only)
Calculation of weighted price index (HL only)
Trade-off between unemployment and inflation (Phillips curve) (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4 for calculations/diagrams, AO3 for evaluation

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Distinguish between equality and equity
Define economic inequality (unequal distribution of income/wealth)
Measure economic inequality using Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient
Define poverty (absolute vs relative)
Measure poverty using single indicators (poverty lines, minimum income) and composite indicators (MPI)
Explain difficulties measuring poverty

Explain causes of inequality/poverty (inequality of opportunity, resource ownership, human capital, discrimination, status/power, tax/benefits policies, globalization, technology, market-based policies)
Evaluate impact of income/wealth inequality on economic growth, living standards, social stability
Explain the role of taxation in reducing inequality (progressive, regressive, proportional; average/marginal rates; direct/indirect taxes)
Evaluate further policies to reduce poverty/inequality (opportunities/human capital, transfer payments, targeted spending, universal basic income, anti-discrimination, minimum wages)
allowed_methods: Diagram: Lorenz curve showing distribution of income and changes
explicit_exclusions: Construction of Lorenz curve from income quintile data (HL only)
Calculation of indirect tax paid from expenditure given rate (HL only)
Calculation of total/average tax rates from data (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO3, AO4 for diagram

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Define monetary policy (control of money supply/interest rates by central bank)
Explain goals of monetary policy (low inflation, low unemployment, reduce business cycle fluctuations, stable environment for growth, external balance)
Explain expansionary/contractionary monetary policies to close deflationary/inflationary gaps

Evaluate effectiveness of monetary policy (constraints: interest rates near zero, low confidence; strengths: incremental, flexible, short lags; strengths/limitations for growth, unemployment, inflation)
allowed_methods: Diagram: AD/AS curves showing expansionary/contractionary monetary policy
explicit_exclusions: Process of money creation by commercial banks (HL only)
Tools of monetary policy (open market operations, reserve requirements, base rate changes, quantitative easing) (HL only)
Demand/supply of money determination of equilibrium interest rates (HL only)
Calculation of real interest rates (AO2, but calculation allowed)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO1, AO2, AO3, AO4 for diagram

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Define fiscal policy (sources of revenue, expenditures)
Explain goals of fiscal policy (low inflation, low unemployment, stable growth, reduce business cycles, equitable income distribution, external balance)
Explain expansionary/contractionary fiscal policies to close deflationary/inflationary gaps

Evaluate effectiveness of fiscal policy (constraints: political pressure, time lags, sustainable debt; strengths: targeting sectors, effective in deep recession; strengths/limitations for growth, unemployment, inflation)
allowed_methods: Diagram: AD/AS curves showing expansionary/contractionary fiscal policy for Keynesian and monetarist/new classical views
explicit_exclusions: Keynesian multiplier (HL only)
Automatic stabilizers (HL only)
Crowding-out effect (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO3, AO4 for diagram

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain goals of supply-side policies (long-term growth, competition/efficiency, reduce labour costs/unemployment, reduce inflation, increase investment incentives)

Explain market-based policies (encourage competition: deregulation, privatization, trade liberalization, anti-monopoly; labour market: reduce union power, unemployment benefits, abolish minimum wages; incentives: income tax cuts, business/capital gains tax cuts)
Explain interventionist policies (education/training, health care, R&D, infrastructure, industrial policies)
Explain demand-side effects of supply-side policies
Explain supply-side effects of fiscal policies

Evaluate effectiveness of supply-side policies (constraints: equity, time lags, vested interests, environmental impact, costs; strengths: improved allocation, no budget burden, direct support for growth sectors; strengths/limitations for growth, unemployment, inflation)
allowed_methods: Diagram: AD/AS model and LRAS curve showing effect of supply-side policies
Diagram: showing minimum wage
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO3, AO4 for diagrams

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain benefits of international trade (increased competition, lower prices, greater choice, resource acquisition, foreign exchange, access to markets, economies of scale, efficient allocation/production)
allowed_methods: Diagram: free trade illustrating exports when world price > domestic price
Diagram: free trade illustrating imports when world price < domestic price
explicit_exclusions: Absolute and comparative advantage (HL only)
Calculation of quantity of exports/imports, import expenditure, export revenue from diagram (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO4 for diagrams

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Analyze effects of tariffs on markets and stakeholders (price, production, consumption, expenditures, revenues, welfare)
Analyze effects of quotas on markets and stakeholders
Analyze effects of subsidies/export subsidies on markets and stakeholders
Explain administrative barriers (standards/regulations)
allowed_methods: Diagram: effect of a tariff on price, production, consumption, expenditures, revenues, welfare
Diagram: effect of a quota
Diagram: effect of a subsidy
explicit_exclusions: Calculation of effects on stakeholders of tariffs/quotas/subsidies from diagram (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO3, AO4 for diagrams

subject: Economics
subtopic: Arguments for and against trade control/protection
learning_objectives: Explain arguments for trade protection (infant industries, national security, health/safety, environmental standards, anti-dumping, unfair competition, balance of payments, government revenue, job protection, ELDC diversification)
Explain arguments against trade protection (misallocation, retaliation, increased costs, higher prices, less choice, reduced efficiency, reduced export competitiveness)
Discuss free trade vs trade protection
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO3

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Define preferential trade agreements (bilateral, regional, multilateral/WTO)
Define trading blocs (free trade areas, customs unions, common markets)
Evaluate advantages/disadvantages of trading blocs
Define monetary union
Describe objectives/functions of the WTO
Explain factors affecting WTO influence (difficulties on services/primary products, unequal bargaining power)
explicit_exclusions: Trade creation/trade diversion (HL only)
Advantages/disadvantages of monetary union (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO1, AO2, AO3

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain floating exchange rates (determination, depreciation/appreciation)
Calculate price of a good in different currencies using exchange rates

Explain factors causing changes in demand/supply for a currency (exports, imports, FDI, portfolio investment, remittances, speculation, relative inflation/interest/growth rates, central bank intervention)
Evaluate consequences of exchange rate changes on inflation, growth, unemployment, current account, living standards
Explain fixed exchange rates (devaluation/revaluation, how maintained)
Explain managed exchange rates (overvalued/undervalued currencies)
allowed_methods: Diagram: exchange rate determination and changes in equilibrium in a floating system
Diagram: how a fixed exchange rate is maintained
Diagram: exchange rate determination in a managed system
Calculation: changes in currency value from data
explicit_exclusions: Fixed vs floating exchange rate systems (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO3, AO4 for diagrams/calculations

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Define balance of payments (credit/debit items, surplus/deficit)
Calculate elements of balance of payments from data

Explain components of balance of payments (current account: goods, services, income, transfers; capital account: transfers, non-produced assets; financial account: FDI, portfolio, reserve assets, official borrowing)
Explain interdependence between accounts (zero balance, credits matched by debits, deficits matched by surpluses)
allowed_methods: Calculation: elements of balance of payments from data
explicit_exclusions: Relationship between current account and exchange rate (HL only)
Relationship between financial account and exchange rate (HL only)
Implications of persistent current account deficit/surplus (HL only)
Methods to correct persistent deficit (HL only)
Marshall-Lerner condition and J-curve (HL only)

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Define sustainable development
Describe Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
explicit_exclusions: Relationship between sustainability and poverty (HL only)
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain the multidimensional nature of economic development
Describe single indicators (GDP/GNI per capita PPP, health/education, inequality, energy, environmental)
Describe composite indicators (HDI, GII, IHDI, Happy Planet Index)
Evaluate strengths/limitations of approaches to measuring development
Discuss possible relationship between economic growth and development
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO3

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain poverty traps/cycles

Explain economic barriers (rising inequality, lack of infrastructure/technology, low human capital, primary sector dependence, lack of market access, informal economy, capital flight, indebtedness, geography, climate/disease)
Explain political/social barriers (weak institutions: legal, tax, banking, property rights; gender inequality; lack of governance/corruption; unequal political power)
Evaluate significance of different barriers
allowed_methods: Diagram: poverty cycle showing linked factors
exam_style_notes: Assessment objective: AO2, AO3, AO4 for diagram

subject: Economics
learning_objectives: Explain strategies to promote growth/development (trade: import substitution, export promotion, integration; diversification; social enterprise; market-based: liberalization, privatization, deregulation; interventionist: redistribution, merit goods provision, infrastructure, industrial policies; inward FDI; foreign aid: humanitarian/development, debt relief, ODA, NGOs; multilateral assistance: World Bank, IMF; institutional change: banking/microfinance, women's empowerment, reducing corruption, property/land rights)
Evaluate strengths/limitations of strategies
Evaluate government intervention vs market-oriented approaches
Evaluate progress toward meeting SDGs in context of two or more countries
